t.E901.agn: In 2005 JECFA, based on its long history of use and the absence of toxicity in its main components, concluded that there is no safety concern at the estimated intake (below 650 mg per person per day); the ADI was stated as 'acceptable'.
t.E901.body: It is generally accepted that waxes are not digested or absorbed in mammals, including humans; beeswax is not broken down by digestive enzymes and does not melt at body temperature. There are no research data directly demonstrating this.
t.E901.found.0: Fruit surface (citrus fruits, melons, apples, pears, peaches, pineapples, bananas, mangoes, avocados, pomegranates)
t.E901.found.1: Confectionery and small chocolate-coated bakery products
t.E901.found.2: Chewing gum, coffee beans, coated nuts and snacks
t.E901.found.4: Carrier in colour and flavouring preparations (in flavoured drinks max. 200 mg/l)
t.E901.regx.0: ADI 'acceptable'; no safety concern at the estimated intake.
t.E901.summary: A natural wax produced by bees. A glazing agent in coatings for confectionery, fruit and cheese.
t.E901.what: A wax obtained from honeybee combs; used as a glazing agent and carrier.
